_comment: Hermes agents that receive skill installs and updates. Edit this file, not the deploy script. `python3 deploy.py --list` shows status; `python3 deploy.py <skill>` delivers to every enabled agent. `authoring: true` means skills may be EDITED there and pushed back — see contribute.py and CONTRIBUTING.md; every other box is install-only and its local edits are overwritten by the next deploy.

agents.notes: Development box and source of truth. Skills are authored here; deploys originate here.

agents.name: jj-amd

agents.name: jj-hp-prodesk
agents.notes: SSH username is 'user' (the Windows default), NOT an estate name. No system Python and no py launcher: only the Microsoft Store alias stub, which prints an install advert and exits 9009 -- use the Hermes venv interpreter in 'python'. Naming: Tailscale DNSName is jj-hp-prodesk, OS COMPUTERNAME is DESKTOP-1H61R6I -- both are this one machine, on the local LAN (192.168.0.107). Do not confuse it with the 'jack-prodesk' node, which is a separate box at a remote site.

agents.name: jack-laptop
agents.blocked_reason: sshd is LISTENING and the box is online on the tailnet (port 22 open, verified 2026-08-30), but every username is denied: publickey,password,keyboard-interactive — tried justi/Justin/justinjohnson/justinjohnson256/jj/hermes/jack. Tailscale SSH is NOT enabled on this node (no advertised host key), so the tailnet identity cannot be used to bypass the key. TO ENABLE, either: (a) append the mac pubkey 'ssh-ed25519 ...Hi3MXt hermes-macmini' to C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys on that box, or (b) run `tailscale set --ssh` there to let the tailnet authenticate. Then confirm the username, set enabled=true, and run deploy.py.
agents.notes: Online and reachable on the tailnet; only authentication blocks it. Hermes presence unconfirmed. Tailnet owner shows as justinjohnson256@.

agents.name: jack-prodesk
agents.blocked_reason: sshd is listening on 22 and answering, but the mac's key is not authorised and the username is unknown -- user/jack/Jack/justi/hp/prodesk/jackp/owner all denied (administrator/Administrator get a connection reset, which is a disabled account, not a wrong name). Fix: on the box, append the mac pubkey to C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys as ASCII with no BOM, icacls /inheritance:r granting only Administrators+SYSTEM, restart sshd, then report `whoami` so the username can be recorded here.
agents.notes: A SEPARATE machine from jj-hp-prodesk, despite reporting the same Windows COMPUTERNAME -- almost certainly deployed from the same image. Proof they are not one host: different SSH host keys (jack-prodesk SHA256:yRLYsvp7VVtsoNroFb5YKJoNQ8uBP6Ng3VAmSzVD/kE vs jj-hp-prodesk SHA256:powDMwNX3Vex1FKTA1HO6P0HCVasmOQW9pBGDxv5Cs0), both online simultaneously, and different networks (this one is remote via public IP 80.79.48.133; jj-hp-prodesk is on the local LAN). Enrolled 2026-08-30. Because the COMPUTERNAME collides, ALWAYS identify these two by tailnet IP or host key, never by hostname. Assume it has the same no-system-Python trap and record a per-agent 'python' path once reachable.
